entries.quote: It chose a fantastic art direction by making them chibi and cute.
entries.why: Argon's chibi characters, as a direction. Ken hasn't named a specific piece as the best example yet.
Koto as a woodblock print and as an ink painting. Ken liked all three directions in the study; the third, hariko, has since been rejected.

entries.quote: I hate the toy aesthetic completely. The red and white and blue designs are fugly.
entries.why: All hariko and painted toy art, in the game and in tests. Asked if that included the game's plan, Ken said "Yes. I hate all of it."

entries.quote: It looks like any regular plain old Home Screen. I dislike it because of how simple it is, it's the first thing our users see. It should be stylized. Creative. It should take risks.
entries.why: A safe, tidied-up Home. Ken loved the content, disliked the format, and asked for a redesign rather than an edit.
Argon's two Home concepts: the scene as the UI, and the emaki scroll. The reasons weren't recorded.

entries.quote: the animations GPT made are much too flashy, I just need a thin white slice effect and damage effect and hurt anim and KO anim and special KO effect.
entries.why: Busy battle effects. Ken wants restraint: a thin slice and clear reactions.

entries.quote: The bushes look a bit rough visually. Like sloppy circles. Same for the walking animation at the beginning, he just bounces.
entries.why: Blobby shapes built from circles, and walking that's only a bounce.
